memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"When the people saw the thunder and lightning and heard the trumpet and saw the
mountain in smoke, they trembled with fear. They stayed at a distance and said to
Moses, 'Speak to us yourself and we will listen. But do not have God speak to us
or we will die.'" - Ex 20:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The people have just heard God speak directly, and their response is: please
stop.

They want a mediator. "Speak to us yourself." Anyone but God directly.

We should not judge them for this. Their instinct was correct. Sinful people
cannot stand in the unmediated presence of a holy God and survive. They were
right to be afraid.

And notice how God responds. Deuteronomy 5:28 records His verdict on this
request: "Everything they said was good." God agreed with them. He was not
offended by their fear. He accepted their need for a go-between.

That is the whole problem the Bible sets out to solve. How can holy God and
sinful people be together? Israel's answer at the mountain was Moses. But Moses
would die, and every priest after him would die too.

Hebrews makes the contrast: "Because Jesus lives forever, he has a permanent
priesthood. Therefore he is able to save completely those who come to God through
him" (Heb 7:24-25).

They asked for a mediator at Sinai. God gave one at Calvary, and He does not die.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you appreciate what it cost for you to be able to approach God?
2. Are you standing at a distance from God when you have been invited near?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for Jesus, my mediator, who brings me near without fear. Amen.
